The bullet points are misleading.  The OEM Samsung filters are BOTH NSF/ANSI 42 and NSF/ANSI 53 certified.  This filter is only NSF/ANSI 42 certified.  This is a big difference in quality.  NSF/ANSI 53 addresses the reduction of specific health-related contaminants such as lead and giardia.  This may not be a big deal for some but an important detail for me.  The reduction of lead provides peace of mind with kids in the house.  I give it one star because the ad is misleading using the statement "Costs less than Samsung without compromising any quality or flow rate."

This is very fast and easy to use. I take one to work since our water at work taste and smells like chlorine. This takes the taste and smell out of it. It saves me the money I would buy on water bottles.
The filters are really easy to change out and they even have a little cutout window to remind you when to change out the filter.

It seems to filter very well but not as quickly as claimed . It does seem to filter out some dissolved solids - the meter I have measures it at 148 ppm which is better than some but also worse than some - the taste of the water is improved a little. You also have to hold your thumb on the cover or it will fall off on top of whatever you are trying to pour into.

When you watch the product video you think you're getting a pitcher with a filter that filters water quite quickly. You don't. Faucet has to be at a trickle in order for the drop filter not to overflow.

The design of the pitcher is fabulous although if you pour the water out too fast the "perfect pour" spout isn't such a small stream anymore; water comes out of the slit where the spout is attached making the stream larger.

Water tastes great, I can't detect any taste at all and I have a pretty sensitive nose and taste buds.

If you don't mind waiting for your water to filter at a snail's pace then I'd recommend this pitcher. Also, if you want the ability to fill other vessels with a portable water filter you may like this.

UPDATE 04.27.2016
Was going to mention this in the earlier review but forgot. I had been drinking the water while it was cold. I drank some of the water later on after it had gotten to room temperature and it had a funny, plastic-y taste so I've deducted one more star.

We mostly buy bottled water or when available fill our water bottles at the machines in front of grocery stores. Occasionally when we're running a bit low and I want to make a pitcher of iced tea I'll use tap water so we still have water. Every time I do I think of all of the current news stories involving dangerous or even poisonous tap water. I figured a filter, any filter, can only help. The fact that this comes with a pitcher and a filter that can be used with the pitcher or with almost anything else you have in the house was a bonus.

The pitcher is a serious disappointment to me. If were rating it alone, it'd get 1 star. The spout that closes for pouring has a gap in that allows water to pour out even when closed -- though it doesn't snap closed so if you bump the pitcher a little the spout flaps all around. The plastic feels cheap. It really need a different lid that doesn't pop off so easily. That's the bad.

The good is the filter itself is easy to use. It can be used in almost any pitcher or bottle you have at home. In fact If it's possible, I'd recommend buying the filter section without the pitcher. It has markings so you can see what month you starting using the filter. Although you CAN filter water fast, if you're not fond of wasting water I'd actually do it at a slower steady stream as the filter itself does not hold a lot of water so a lot of water is literally going down the drain as it pours out over the filter. This is a nice looking filter pitcher, however, it takes up a lot more space on my fridge shelf than the narrow Brita pitcher I have. The only way to let this fill directly from the faucet is with a very thin stream of water. I have always just filled the reservoir of the Brita, then put it in the fridge to drip down. This one requires watching. I did a "taste test" of this pitcher and the Brita and found no difference. It looks like the replacement filters for this are pretty pricey, and not sure of how available. Perhaps the funnel that can be used in other containers makes it worthwhile. It is attractive, nice design.

The pros: it removes chlorine smell and taste from our city water. The pitcher is attractive for serving use. The pour spout rocks - it has a little self-opening flip-top cover, and it pours quickly without dripping. That, and the cover for the filtration section, would help keep insects out if using this outdoors.

The cons: it would be nice to have some kind of marks indicating cups on the pitcher, for filling our teakettle with an appropriate amount of water for our teapots. The filtration is rather slow, but not more so than other similar devices; however, because of the size of the filtration space, one must keep the unit under the faucet for an extended period of time. It's a tall pitcher, so if you have a low faucet, this could be an issue. I would not want to hold the filtration device in my hand to fill another container because it would be so time-consuming. I used to own a Britta and one could fill the top reservoir and then set the pitcher down, and the filtration part would just work at it's own speed. With this pitcher, you must control the faucet water flow and keep it very low.

I cannot find any indication of what other particles the filter might remove from our water, and I would like to know. All it mentions is chlorine.

While I like the design of the pitcher, the filtration doesn't work well enough for me. The water where I live has terrible water, and although I did notice a slight improvement, it still tastes horrible. I didn't have any problems filling it and it's kinda neat that the filter can be used with other Whirlpool products, but I'm just iffy on the whole thing. Maybe if I lived in a place where the water was better, I'd give it a go, but it's just not doing it here, so I'll be sticking to buying RO (Reverse Osmosis) water from the machines. But hey, at least I have another pitcher.

Compared to the brita, I like this better. It is nice to be able to use the filter on anything. You can use it to just make 1 glass or set it over your coffee maker when making coffee.
